topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students, introduces complement as the lecture subject, and frames its complexity and importance.

topics.label: Fundamentals of the Complement System and C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational principles of complement, explaining its general architecture, naming conventions, and the central role of C3.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three recognition pathways—alternative, lectin, and classical—that initiate complement activation and converge on C3 deposition.

topics.label: Complement Effector Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three downstream effector functions triggered by complement activation to eliminate pathogens: opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical Consequences of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how genetic and acquired deficiencies in specific complement proteins result in distinct clinical disease presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the strategies evolved by pathogens, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, to circumvent and neutralize complement activity.

topics.label: Closing Remarks and Next Lecture Preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture on complement and outlines the topic of the upcoming lecture in the series.
